summary.title: Educational STRIDE Threat Model — Network-Connected CT Scanner
summary.description: Educational threat model for a network-connected CT scanner and its connected clinical ecosystem. Purpose: demonstrate STRIDE-based threat identification using an OWASP Threat Dragon DFD. This is not a product security certification, regulatory submission, clinical safety assessment, penetration-test report, or formal manufacturer cybersecurity risk assessment. Product-specific evidence is limited to the Siemens Healthineers DICOM Conformance Statement, syngo CT VB20A, Revision 4.2, dated 07/01/2026. Product documentation identifies documented capabilities; deployment configuration and observed behaviour are separate evidence states. Optional or conditional features are not treated as deployed unless confirmed. Clinical consequences are not inferred without device, deployment, workflow, and safety evidence.

threats.title: T21 Insufficient audit attribution
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: V-P/D; Priority: Medium] Security-relevant actions cannot be reliably attributed to the initiating user, service identity or system.
threats.mitigation: Define required audit events and identity sources; verify that relevant events contain sufficient attribution and timestamps.

threats.title: T22 Audit record modification, deletion or loss
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: V-P/D; Priority: Medium] Audit records are modified, deleted, redirected or unavailable when needed for investigation.
threats.mitigation: Restrict audit access, protect audit storage/transmission and verify retention and integrity controls for the deployment.

threats.title: T34 Unauthorized DICOM autorouting change
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: V-P/D; Priority: High] Autorouting rules or destinations are changed so that DICOM instances are sent to an unauthorized or unintended destination.
threats.mitigation: Restrict autorouting configuration, review destinations and rules, authorize changes and audit configuration activity.

threats.title: T37 Long-term cryptographic obsolescence / PQC migration risk
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: U; Priority: Medium] Cryptographic mechanisms used by the CT or its connected deployment may become deprecated, unsupported or unsuitable during an approximately 10-year lifecycle. If applicable cryptographic functions cannot be migrated or replaced, long-lived sensitive information may face future confidentiality risk, including a potential harvest-now-decrypt-later scenario. Public-key cryptography used for authentication, certificates, key establishment or software/firmware signing may also require future migration. This threat does not establish that the particular CT product is currently vulnerable to a quantum attack.
threats.mitigation: Maintain an inventory of security-relevant cryptographic mechanisms; assess cryptographic agility, certificate/key replacement, authorized software/firmware update capability and vendor migration support; define a lifecycle migration plan when applicable standards or security requirements change.

threats.title: T32 Unauthorized access to CT local storage
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] Patient or imaging data stored locally on the CT is accessed by an unauthorized user, process or maintenance path.
threats.mitigation: Restrict local and administrative access, protect stored data as supported and verify access controls in deployment testing.

threats.title: T33 Unauthorized modification of CT local storage
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] Stored patient or imaging data is modified or deleted without authorization.
threats.mitigation: Restrict storage access, protect administrative paths and verify integrity and recovery behavior using approved test data.

threats.title: T01 Unauthorized DICOM peer impersonation
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] An unauthorized endpoint presents itself as an approved DICOM peer for CT-to-PACS communication.
threats.mitigation: Restrict DICOM peers using approved AE/IP configuration and network ACLs; use TLS with appropriate peer authentication where supported and configured.

threats.title: T02 DICOM object or metadata tampering in transit
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] DICOM objects or metadata are modified in transit before reaching the intended destination.
threats.mitigation: Protect sensitive DICOM links with configured secure transport where supported; restrict network paths and validate received data in the receiving workflow.

threats.title: T03 DICOM information disclosure
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] Patient and imaging information in DICOM traffic may be exposed to an unauthorized network observer.
threats.mitigation: Use protected DICOM transport where supported and configured and restrict the network path to authorized systems.

threats.title: T04 DICOM service disruption
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] An unauthorized host or network condition disrupts CT-to-PACS DICOM communication.
threats.mitigation: Use network segmentation, ACLs and monitoring; validate resilience with controlled non-production methods rather than flooding a clinical CT.

threats.title: T05 Unauthorized DICOM sender impersonation
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] An unauthorized endpoint presents itself as an approved sender of DICOM objects to the CT.
threats.mitigation: Restrict inbound DICOM peers and ports; use approved AE/IP configuration and secure peer authentication where supported.

threats.title: T06 Malicious or altered DICOM object accepted by CT
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] A connected system sends an altered or malicious DICOM object to the CT and the object is accepted or processed unexpectedly.
threats.mitigation: Restrict inbound DICOM associations to approved peers and validate object handling; assess input validation and negative cases in controlled testing.

threats.title: T07 Unauthorized DICOM retrieval or receipt
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] An unauthorized peer obtains or causes delivery of patient or imaging data from the CT.
threats.mitigation: Restrict Query/Retrieve and Storage peers; authorize destinations and retrieve operations; monitor relevant audit records where available.

threats.title: T08 DICOM resource exhaustion
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] Excessive or malformed DICOM requests consume resources and reduce service availability.
threats.mitigation: Use network access controls, rate/resource controls where available, monitoring and safe non-production testing; do not intentionally exhaust resources on a clinical scanner.

threats.title: T09 Storage Commitment peer impersonation
threats.description: [Impact: Medium; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: V-P/D; Priority: Medium] An unauthorized endpoint impersonates a configured Storage Commitment peer.
threats.mitigation: Restrict Storage Commitment associations to approved peers and verify the configured destination and transport protection.

threats.title: T10 Storage Commitment status manipulation
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] A false or altered Storage Commitment interaction causes the workflow to treat data as committed when the intended storage state is not established.
threats.mitigation: Restrict peers and validate Storage Commitment state transitions and failure handling in controlled testing.

threats.title: T11 Query/Retrieve peer impersonation
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] An unauthorized endpoint impersonates a configured Query/Retrieve peer.
threats.mitigation: Restrict Query/Retrieve peers and verify AE/IP configuration and transport protection.

threats.title: T12 Unauthorized Query/Retrieve access
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] An unauthorized peer queries or retrieves patient or imaging information.
threats.mitigation: Authorize Query/Retrieve peers and operations, restrict network reachability and audit relevant activity where supported.

threats.title: T13 Query/Retrieve service disruption
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] Query/Retrieve requests or network conditions make the service unavailable to authorized clinical workflows.
threats.mitigation: Use ACLs, segmentation and monitoring; use controlled non-production tests for resource exhaustion.

threats.title: T14 Modality Worklist provider impersonation
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: V-P/D; Priority: High] An unauthorized system presents itself as the configured Worklist provider.
threats.mitigation: Restrict Worklist associations to approved peers and verify AE/IP configuration and transport protection.

threats.title: T15 Modality Worklist tampering
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] Patient or procedure information returned by the Worklist service is altered or replaced before use.
threats.mitigation: Protect the Worklist connection and peer identity; validate patient/procedure association and investigate unexpected Worklist values.

threats.title: T16 Modality Worklist information disclosure
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] Worklist responses expose patient or procedure information to an unauthorized observer.
threats.mitigation: Use protected transport where supported and configured and restrict the Worklist network path.

threats.title: T17 Modality Worklist availability failure
threats.description: [Impact: Medium; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] Loss or disruption of the Worklist service prevents or degrades the expected registration workflow.
threats.mitigation: Define and test approved degraded-workflow behavior and monitor Worklist service availability.

threats.title: T18 MPPS peer impersonation
threats.description: [Impact: Medium; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: V-P/D; Priority: Medium] An unauthorized endpoint impersonates the configured MPPS destination.
threats.mitigation: Restrict MPPS associations to approved peers and verify configuration and transport protection.

threats.title: T19 MPPS status tampering
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] MPPS status information is altered or accepted from an unauthorized source, affecting workflow state.
threats.mitigation: Restrict MPPS peers, protect transport where supported and validate state handling.

threats.title: T20 MPPS information disclosure
threats.description: [Impact: Medium; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] MPPS traffic exposes patient or procedure information to an unauthorized observer.
threats.mitigation: Use protected transport where supported and configured and restrict the MPPS network path.

cells.description: Local clinical interaction with the CT; authentication and privilege controls are deployment-dependent.

threats.title: T25 Unauthorized CT administrative privilege
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] A user or connected system gains administrative capability beyond its authorized role.
threats.mitigation: Apply least privilege, strong administrative authentication and controlled service access; review administrative paths and permissions.

threats.title: T26 Unauthorized CT configuration change
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] Security, DICOM, network or workflow configuration is changed without authorization.
threats.mitigation: Restrict configuration access, authorize changes, maintain change records and review configuration after maintenance.

threats.title: T27 Configuration information disclosure
threats.description: [Impact: Medium; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] Configuration information such as peer definitions, network settings or service parameters is disclosed to an unauthorized party.
threats.mitigation: Restrict configuration access and protect exported configuration data and administrative interfaces.

cells.description: Maintenance path exists only where the deployment enables or permits such access.

threats.title: T28 Unauthorized software or firmware change
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] Software or firmware is modified or installed without an authorized update process.
threats.mitigation: Require authenticated/authorized update mechanisms, verify update provenance and integrity, restrict update privileges and retain update records.

threats.title: T29 Unauthorized maintenance access
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] A maintenance path is used by an unauthorized person or system to gain privileged access to the CT.
threats.mitigation: Control maintenance access by role, approval and time; use authenticated channels and audit maintenance activity.

threats.title: T30 Maintenance data disclosure
threats.description: [Impact: Medium; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] Patient, configuration or security information is exposed through a maintenance or service path.
threats.mitigation: Limit maintenance data access and transfer, use secure channels and avoid unnecessary patient data exposure during service.

cells.description: Examples documented by the product include NTP/SNTP, DHCP, DNS and LDAP; the actual services used by a deployment must be confirmed.

threats.title: T23 Supporting service impersonation or manipulation
threats.description: [Impact: Medium; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: V-P/D; Priority: Medium] A supporting network service used by the deployment is impersonated or manipulated, affecting name resolution, time, addressing or directory-related functions.
threats.mitigation: Document which supporting services are actually used; restrict trusted service endpoints and use appropriate secure mechanisms for each deployed service.

threats.title: T24 Supporting service disruption
threats.description: [Impact: Medium; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] Loss or disruption of a supporting network service affects an operational workflow.
threats.mitigation: Identify required dependencies, define degraded behavior and monitor service availability.

cells.description: Represents network reachability to CT services from other connected systems; exact allowed sources and ports are deployment-dependent.

threats.title: T31 Compromised connected system used as a trusted pathway
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] A compromised connected system with legitimate network reachability is used to reach CT services or act through an implicitly trusted relationship.
threats.mitigation: Segment the CT, restrict allowed peers and ports, minimize trust relationships and monitor unexpected connections.

threats.title: T35 Unauthorized host reaches CT services
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Medium; Evidence: D/U; Priority: High] A host that is not an approved CT peer can reach exposed CT network services.
threats.mitigation: Enforce network ACLs/firewall rules and approved-peer allow-lists; verify reachability from authorized and unauthorized test hosts.

threats.title: T36 Network flooding or service disruption
threats.description: [Impact: High; Exploitability: Low; Evidence: D/U; Priority: Medium] Excessive network traffic or an upstream failure disrupts communication needed by the CT workflow.
threats.mitigation: Use segmentation, ACLs, capacity monitoring and defined degraded operation; do not perform destructive flooding on a clinical device.

requirements.R01: DICOM peers shall be authorized and restricted to approved communication partners.
requirements.R02: Sensitive DICOM communication shall use appropriate protection where required by the deployment.
requirements.R03: Security-relevant actions shall be sufficiently auditable for the intended environment.
requirements.R04: Patient, imaging, configuration, and security-relevant information shall be protected from unauthorized disclosure.
requirements.R05: Supporting network services shall be restricted to approved infrastructure and maintained for required availability.
requirements.R06: Administrative and service privileges shall be limited to authorized personnel and functions.
requirements.R07: Software and firmware update mechanisms shall protect authenticity and integrity.
requirements.R08: Maintenance and vendor access shall be controlled and auditable.
requirements.R09: Security, DICOM, network, and autorouting configuration shall be protected against unauthorized change.
requirements.R10: Patient, procedure, and workflow information shall be protected against unauthorized modification or substitution.
requirements.R11: Network-degraded behaviour shall be defined and assessed for the deployment.
requirements.R12: Trust boundaries shall restrict unauthorized communication paths into the CT environment.
requirements.R13: Autorouting destinations and forwarding rules shall be authorized, reviewed, and protected against unauthorized change.
requirements.R14: Cybersecurity threats that could affect device safety or essential performance shall be evaluated for their potential to contribute to an uncontrolled clinical hazard.
requirements.R15: Where a cybersecurity threat can contribute to a clinical safety hazard, the cybersecurity mitigation shall be traceable to the corresponding product safety risk control and verification/validation evidence.
requirements.R16: Cybersecurity risk evaluation shall distinguish controlled residual risk from uncontrolled risk requiring appropriate remediation.
requirements.R17: Security mitigations shall be reviewed for their effect on existing safety controls and shall not introduce an unacceptable new safety risk.
requirements.R18: The threat-model record shall maintain bidirectional traceability between relevant cybersecurity threats, safety hazards, controls, applicable risk-management records, and verification/validation evidence where a clinical-safety relationship exists.
requirements.R19: Cryptographic agility and lifecycle migration should be assessed for security-relevant communications, authentication, certificates, key establishment, software/firmware protection and maintenance functions so that applicable cryptographic mechanisms can be replaced or upgraded as standards and security requirements evolve.

validation.V21: Long-term cryptographic migration review: inventory deployed cryptographic protocols, algorithms, certificates and key-establishment/signature functions; review cryptographic agility, certificate/key replacement, authorized software/firmware update capability and vendor migration support; document whether a practical PQC migration path exists.

risk_fields.note: Qualitative discussion/prioritization fields; not an objective numerical calculation and not an FDA-mandated scoring method.

assumptions: The DFD represents a representative connected CT deployment.
PACS and RIS/HIS are external systems to the CT threat boundary.
Supporting network services are represented separately.
Actual enabled services, peers, ports, TLS settings, routing rules, audit destinations, and maintenance paths require deployment confirmation.
Network attack does not automatically imply manipulation of CT acquisition parameters or patient harm.
Network outage does not automatically imply patient harm.
The educational model considers an approximately 10-year operational lifecycle for future-oriented analysis only; actual device service life is deployment/manufacturer dependent.

post_quantum_cryptography.lifecycle_context: This model considers an expected operational lifecycle of approximately 10 years as a future-oriented threat-modeling assumption. This does not establish the actual service life of a particular CT deployment.
post_quantum_cryptography.threat_modeling_boundary: PQC is treated as a long-term cryptographic lifecycle and migration risk, not as evidence that a cryptographically relevant quantum computer currently exists or that the particular CT product is presently vulnerable.
post_quantum_cryptography.risk_scenario: Cryptographic mechanisms used for CT communications, authentication, certificates, software or firmware protection, maintenance connections, or other security functions may become deprecated, unsupported, or unsuitable during the device lifecycle. If the device or deployment cannot migrate or replace applicable cryptographic mechanisms, long-lived sensitive information may face future confidentiality risk and security functions relying on public-key cryptography may face future integrity or authentication risk.
post_quantum_cryptography.harvest_now_decrypt_later: Encrypted network traffic containing information with a long confidentiality lifetime may be captured now and potentially decrypted later if currently used quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography becomes breakable. This is a lifecycle consideration, not evidence of current compromise.
crypto_agility: Identify cryptographic protocols and algorithms used by the device and deployment.
Identify where public-key cryptography is used for confidentiality, authentication, certificates, key establishment, digital signatures, software or firmware protection, and maintenance.
Determine whether certificates and keys can be replaced without inappropriate hardware replacement.
Determine whether firmware/software and cryptographic components can be updated through an authorized and integrity-protected process.
Assess whether the product and deployment have a practical migration path when approved cryptographic standards or protocol requirements change.
Record vendor information about planned post-quantum migration support where available.
post_quantum_cryptography.current_evidence_boundary: The Siemens DICOM Conformance Statement documents TLS 1.2 and secure transport configuration, but that documentation alone does not establish the exact deployed cryptographic algorithms, certificates, key exchange configuration, cryptographic agility, or PQC capability.
post_quantum_cryptography.pqc_algorithm_boundary: This model does not require a particular PQC algorithm for the CT. NIST has finalized ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA standards, but applicability to the CT product, DICOM/TLS implementation, certificate infrastructure, and medical-device lifecycle must be assessed before specifying a particular implementation.
post_quantum_cryptography.external_reference: NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography guidance and standards are used as technical lifecycle context.
